contentHtml:
Hiring software engineers in India: the short answer

In short: Most of what decides whether an engineer joins and stays sits in your offer letter, not in a statute: notice period, probation, non-compete wording and the first 90 days. The law sets a floor you must know: appointment letters are now mandatory under the labour codes in force since 21 November 2025, a non-compete after someone leaves is void under section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, and final wages are due within two working days of a resignation under the Code on Wages.

I wrote this for founders and engineering managers in India who are hiring their first few developers, or replacing people who left too soon. It covers what the law actually says, what you are free to decide yourself, and a hiring process that makes the second part work.

This guide was checked in November 2026, against the Press Information Bureau release on the four labour codes, the text of the Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and the Code on Wages, 2019 on PRS Legislative Research, the Telangana Shops and Establishments Act, 1988, and section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. I am not a lawyer. Treat this as a map for the conversation with your HR or labour consultant, not a substitute for it.

What the law decides and what your offer letter decides

Founders often assume there is a legal rule for every hiring question. There are fewer than you think, and the ones that exist matter a lot.

What Indian law sets for a software engineer's employment, and what is left to the contract

QuestionWhat the law saysWhere it comes fromLeft to you
Do I need a written appointment letter?Yes, appointment letters are mandatory for all workersPIB release on the labour codes, effective 21 November 2025What goes in it, beyond the basics
When is salary due?For monthly pay, before the end of the seventh day of the next monthCode on Wages, 2019, section 17(1)The pay date, as long as it is on or before that
When is the final settlement due after resignation?Wages within two working days of the resignationCode on Wages, 2019, section 17(2)How you run the exit process
Can I stop them joining a competitor after they leave?An agreement restraining a lawful profession is void to that extentIndian Contract Act, 1872, section 27Confidentiality and IP clauses, which are a different thing
How long is probation?No single number for a small software firm; standing orders that list probationers apply at 300 or more workersIndustrial Relations Code, 2020, section 28 and First ScheduleLength, review and what happens at the end
How much notice must they give?Telangana's Act asks an employee who resigns for at least 15 days, or forfeits 15 days of service compensationTelangana Shops and Establishments Act, 1988, section 47The contractual notice period and any buyout
Gratuity for fixed-term hiresPayable after one year of continuous servicePIB release on the labour codesWhether you hire on fixed terms at all

Source: PIB, four labour codes made effective and Code on Wages, 2019 and Industrial Relations Code, 2020 and Indian Contract Act, section 27 and Telangana Shops and Establishments Act, 1988, read 16 November 2026.

Two cautions on that table. First, DLA Piper's note on the codes says all four are effective from 21 November 2025, but certain provisions of some codes are yet to be brought into effect, and the state rules that fill in detail are still arriving. Second, the Telangana row is a state law, and other states have their own shops and establishments acts with different numbers. If your team sits in Bengaluru or Pune, read that state's Act, not this one.

The labour codes, in the parts that touch a tech hire

On 21 November 2025 the government made the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 effective. The PIB release says they rationalise 29 existing labour laws.

The same release has a section on IT and ITES workers. It lists release of salary mandatory by the 7th of every month, equal pay for equal work, and annual leave after 180 days of work in a year. For a startup that has been paying "around the 10th, when the client pays us", that first line is the one to fix this month.

The release also says that fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after one year of continuous service, instead of five. If you hire engineers on one-year contracts to keep commitments light, price that in. The Industrial Relations Code also says a fixed-term worker's hours, wages, allowances and other benefits shall not be less than those of a permanent worker doing the same or similar work. So a fixed-term contract is no longer a cheaper version of a permanent one.

Is a software engineer a worker under the codes?

This sounds academic. It decides whether a lot of the Industrial Relations Code applies to your hire.

Section 2(zr) of the Industrial Relations Code defines a worker as a person employed to do manual, unskilled, skilled, technical, operational, clerical or supervisory work. It then excludes a person employed mainly in a managerial or administrative capacity, and a person in a supervisory capacity drawing wages above ₹18,000 a month (or an amount the Central Government notifies). A developer writing code is doing technical work, so read the definition with your consultant before you assume your engineers are outside it.

The Code on Wages uses a wider word. Its definition of employee includes supervisory, managerial, administrative and technical work. So the wage timing rules in section 17 cover your senior engineers and your engineering manager too.

Standing orders are where probation lives in law. Section 28 of the Industrial Relations Code applies that chapter to industrial establishments with 300 or more workers. The First Schedule lists what standing orders must cover, starting with classification of workers as permanent, temporary, apprentices, probationers, badlis or fixed term, and including termination and the notice to be given by employer and workers. A ten-person startup is well below that threshold, which is why its probation and notice rules come from the offer letter.

Notice periods: what Telangana's Act says

Most of our readers hire in Hyderabad, so here is the state law there. Section 47 of the Telangana Shops and Establishments Act, 1988 covers termination and resignation.

  • If you end the job: for an employee in continuous employment for at least six months, you need a reasonable cause and at least one month's notice in writing or wages in lieu. Every termination must be in writing, with a copy to the Inspector within three days.
  • Service compensation: after at least one year of continuous employment, fifteen days' average wages for each year, including on resignation. It does not apply where gratuity has been paid under the Payment of Gratuity Act.
  • If they resign: the employee may leave after giving at least fifteen days' notice. Without that notice, the service compensation payable is forfeited to the extent of fifteen days.

Notice what that last line does and does not say. The statute's own number for an employee's resignation is fifteen days. If your offer letter asks for longer, that is a contractual term you have chosen, and how far it can be enforced is a question for your lawyer, not for a blog. What I would take from it is practical: a long notice period is a promise the engineer makes to you, and it holds only as well as the relationship does.

Telangana has also issued exemption orders under the Act over the years. One example: Nishith Desai Associates reports an October 2022 notification letting establishments in Telangana employ women on night shifts between 8:30 pm and 6 am, subject to conditions. If your office runs late shifts for a US client, check which current orders apply to you.

Non-compete clauses: why most are dead weight

Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 says every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind is, to that extent, void. The only statutory exception is for someone who sells the goodwill of a business.

So a clause saying "you will not work for any competitor for two years after leaving" protects you less than it seems to. What does protect you is different and fully in your control:

  • Confidentiality: what they may not disclose, during and after employment.
  • Intellectual property assignment: code, designs and documents created in the job belong to the company. Get this signed on day one, not when someone resigns.
  • Access hygiene: company accounts for GitHub, cloud and email, so access can be removed in minutes. This matters more than any clause.
  • Non-solicitation of clients or staff: narrower than a non-compete. Ask your lawyer how your wording is likely to be read.

Step by step: a hiring process for engineers who stay

The legal floor is short. The rest is process. Here is the order I would run it in for a small team.

Step 1. Write the role as outcomes. Not "React developer with 3 to 5 years". Write what this person will have shipped by month three and month six. "Owns the patient booking flow in our app, including the payment step" tells a candidate whether they want the job and tells you how to interview.

Step 2. Fix the salary band before the first call. Decide the range, and whether you will match a counter-offer. A good candidate may be holding more than one offer while serving notice, so a band you can defend in week one saves you a renegotiation in week six.

Step 3. Interview for the work, not for trivia. A short, paid task drawn from your real backlog, or a pairing session on your own code, shows how someone reads unfamiliar code and asks questions. Keep it to a few hours and say up front what you will pay.

Step 4. Let them meet the team they will work with. The person most likely to make them stay or leave is their lead. Put that person in the loop, and let the candidate ask about how code review and releases actually work.

Step 5. Send a complete offer letter. Role, pay and pay date, probation length and what is reviewed at the end of it, notice period both ways, confidentiality and IP assignment, leave, and where they will work. The labour codes make the written letter mandatory, so make it a good one.

Step 6. Stay in touch during their notice period. This is where offers die. A weekly message, an invite to a team lunch, early access to the repository README. Say plainly that you expect counter-offers and that you would rather hear about one than be surprised on joining day.

Step 7. Run a planned first 90 days. A laptop and accounts ready on day one, a first small change merged in week one, a named buddy, and a 30, 60 and 90 day check-in with written notes.

Step 8. End probation with a real conversation. Review against the outcomes from Step 1. Confirm in writing. If it is not working, say so before the end date, in writing, and follow the notice terms you set.

Three worked examples

The businesses, numbers and timelines below are illustrative, made up to show the reasoning. The legal points are from the sources above.

A clinic chain hiring its first in-house developer

Say a Hyderabad clinic group with four branches has had an agency build its booking app and now wants one developer to own it. The founder's instinct is a 90-day notice period and a two-year non-compete "so they don't go to a rival hospital".

I would drop the non-compete, given section 27, and put the effort into an IP assignment, company-owned accounts for the Play Console and the cloud, and a written handover document the agency produces before it steps back. I would set notice at a length the founder can live with if the developer resigns, and plan for the case where they leave anyway: two people, not one, who know how to ship a release. Probation of three to six months, with review against "can ship a fix to the booking flow without the agency".

A D2C brand hiring two mobile engineers

Say a skincare brand selling through its own app is hiring two React Native engineers, one senior and one mid-level, while a festive sale is eight weeks out.

The risk here is the notice period gap. If both candidates are serving long notice, they arrive after the sale. I would hire the senior first and keep the agency on a short support contract until both have shipped a release. Both offers would state the pay date on or before the 7th, because the codes now require it for monthly pay. And I would keep the interview task close to the real work: "fix this checkout bug in a copy of our app" tells you more than a whiteboard round.

A coaching institute building a small product team

Say a NEET coaching institute in Vijayawada wants a team of three: a backend developer, a mobile developer and a tester, some on one-year fixed-term contracts to keep commitments flexible.

Under the labour codes, those fixed-term hires get gratuity after one year of continuous service and the same hours, wages and benefits as a permanent worker doing similar work. So the fixed-term route saves less than it used to. I would offer permanent roles with a clear probation, and use fixed terms only where the work really ends, such as a one-off migration. Because this team is in Andhra Pradesh, I would also read that state's shops and establishments law rather than Telangana's.

Mistakes that make engineers leave in the first year

None of these are legal problems. All of them show up in exit conversations.

  • The job is not the one described. Hired to build features, spending the month on support calls. Step 1 exists to stop this.
  • No code review, or code review as punishment. Good engineers want feedback that is fast and about the code. See our guide to code review that helps.
  • Pay that arrives late or changes without a conversation. The 7th-of-the-month rule makes the first one a compliance issue too.
  • No path to ship. If releases need the founder's personal approval at midnight, the engineer is not shipping, they are waiting.
  • Probation that ends in silence. No review, no confirmation letter. People read silence as doubt.
  • Every problem blamed on the last developer. New hires hear that and wonder what will be said about them. Talk about the code, not the person.

Some of those come down to how the codebase itself is run. Our posts on talking about technical debt and code review that helps go deeper on both.

When hiring is not the right answer yet

If you need one app built and then maintained lightly, a full-time hire can be the expensive option. The choice between a freelancer, an agency and your own team has its own trade-offs, which I set out in our post on freelance versus an app development company.

A middle path is to start with an outside team and hire once the product is live and the work is steady. ElevateBox works that way with clients: code, cloud and credentials stay in the client's name from day one, so an in-house hire can take over without a migration. If you want the scope written down before deciding, our ₹3,500 requirement analysis is a call with the people who would build it, ending in a written fixed quotation and timeline (book one here). Hiring in-house later is then a handover, not a rescue.

A hiring checklist you can reuse

Run this for every engineering hire. It takes an hour to set up once.

  1. Role written as three-month and six-month outcomes.
  2. Salary band and counter-offer stance agreed before the first call.
  3. Paid, short, real-work task, with the pay stated up front.
  4. Candidate meets their lead and one future teammate.
  5. Offer letter covers role, pay, pay date on or before the 7th, probation and its review, notice both ways, confidentiality, IP assignment, leave and location.
  6. Fixed-term contracts only where the work really ends, with gratuity after one year priced in.
  7. No post-employment non-compete leaned on as protection; access control and IP assignment instead.
  8. Weekly contact during their notice period.
  9. Day-one laptop, accounts and a buddy. First change merged in week one.
  10. 30, 60 and 90 day check-ins written down. Probation confirmed in writing.
  11. On exit, final wages within two working days of the resignation, and access removed the same day.

Frequently asked questions

There is no single national number for a software engineer at a small company. Telangana's Shops and Establishments Act gives fifteen days as the employee's minimum notice on resignation. A longer notice period in your offer letter is a contractual term, and how far it can be enforced is a question for your lawyer.

Is a non-compete clause enforceable in India?

The exception in the Act covers someone who sells the goodwill of a business. Confidentiality and IP assignment clauses are a different matter and are what you should rely on.

Are appointment letters mandatory now?

Yes. The PIB release on the four labour codes, effective 21 November 2025, lists mandatory appointment letters to all workers. Put the role, pay, pay date, probation, notice and IP terms in writing.

Under section 17 of the Code on Wages, monthly wages are due before the end of the seventh day of the following month, and on resignation the wages payable are due within two working days. Check with your consultant which state rules apply alongside.

How long should probation be for a software engineer?

The law does not set one length for a small software firm. Standing orders that classify probationers apply to establishments with 300 or more workers. I would set three to six months, with a written review against the outcomes you hired for.

Do fixed-term employees get gratuity?

Yes. The PIB release says fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after one year of continuous service, instead of five. The Industrial Relations Code also requires their wages and benefits to be no less than a permanent worker doing similar work.

Does the Telangana Shops and Establishments Act apply to my startup?
